title: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life

learn.hook: Nani picks tiny stones out of the dal before cooking. She's doing science: separating a mixture!
points: A mixture has two or more substances mixed together. We separate them to remove unwanted or harmful parts, or to get useful parts.
Handpicking: picking out by hand things that are big enough to see and few in number, like stones from rice or dal.
Threshing: separating grains from their stalks by beating them, using animals, or using threshing machines.
Winnowing: dropping a mixture from a height in the wind. Light husk blows away; heavy grains fall close by. A soop (winnowing basket) is often used.
Sieving: passing a mixture through a sieve (chhalni). Fine particles pass through; bigger ones stay behind, like bran from flour or pebbles from sand.

example.q: Grandpa has a sack of wheat grains mixed with light, dry husk. Which method should he use, and how does it work?
steps: The husk is much lighter than the grains.
Winnowing uses wind to separate light and heavy parts.
He drops the mixture slowly from a height on a windy day: husk blows away, grains fall in a heap below.

learn.reallife: At a construction site, workers pass sand through a big slanting wire sieve to remove pebbles. At home, flour is sieved before making rotis.

quiz.q: Which method is best to remove a few small stones from rice?
quiz.explain: The stones are few and easy to see, so they can be picked out by hand.
quiz.mistake: Picks a method meant for liquids or for light particles

quiz.q: What is threshing?
quiz.explain: Threshing beats the harvested stalks so the grains come off.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up threshing with winnowing

quiz.q: In winnowing, why does the husk fly away?
options: It is heavier than the grains
It is lighter than the grains
quiz.explain: The wind carries the light husk away, while heavy grains fall down near the person.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the heavier part is blown away

quiz.q: Which tool is used for sieving flour at home?
quiz.explain: A chhalni has tiny holes that let fine flour pass and stop the bran.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the sieve with the winnowing basket

quiz.q: Why do we need to separate substances from a mixture?
options: To remove unwanted or harmful parts and to get useful ones
quiz.explain: We remove stones from dal and husk from grain so food is clean and useful.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the purpose of separation

quiz.q: At a construction site, workers separate pebbles from sand by:
quiz.explain: Sand passes through the holes of a big sieve, and pebbles stay behind.
quiz.mistake: Picks a method that would take too long or does not fit

quiz.q: Which method needs wind to work?
quiz.explain: Winnowing uses moving air to carry away the light husk.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up winnowing and sieving

quiz.q: Handpicking is useful only when:
options: The substance is dissolved in water
The unwanted pieces are big enough to see and are few
There is a lot of wind
quiz.explain: We can pick by hand only things we can see and that are not too many.
quiz.mistake: Thinks handpicking works for dissolved or very tiny particles

teach.ask: Gappu has a bowl of seeds mixed with husk and a few pebbles: 'How do I clean my lunch? I can't pick every bit of husk!'
teach.praise: Tweet! Winnow to blow away the light husk, and handpick the few pebbles. My lunch is clean!
teach.nudge: Which part is lighter, the husk or the seeds? How can the wind help?

learn.hook: Muddy water from a village pond can be made clearer, step by step. Let's see how!
points: Sedimentation: when muddy water is left undisturbed, the heavier insoluble particles slowly settle at the bottom. The settled layer is called sediment.
Decantation: gently pouring off the clearer water from the top without disturbing the sediment.
Filtration: passing a mixture through a filter that lets the liquid pass but stops the solid particles. Examples: tea strainer, filter paper, a clean cotton cloth.
The clear liquid that passes through is called the filtrate; the solid left behind is the residue.
Filtered water may still have germs that we cannot see. It must be boiled or purified before drinking.

example.q: While making paneer, Ammi adds lemon juice to hot milk (adult job!). Soft lumps form in a watery liquid. How can the paneer be separated?
steps: The lumps (chhena) are solid; the watery part (whey) is liquid.
Pour the mixture through a clean muslin cloth.
The whey passes through; the paneer stays in the cloth.

learn.reallife: Tea is filtered through a strainer every morning. Water purifiers at home and big water treatment plants use settling and filtering before cleaning the water further.

games.title: Clean the muddy water
items: Pour muddy water into a glass
Leave it undisturbed so mud settles (sedimentation)

items.text: The layer of mud that settles at the bottom is called ___.
Pouring off the clear water without disturbing the mud is ___.
The clear liquid that passes through a filter is the ___.

quiz.q: What is sedimentation?
options: Heavier insoluble particles settling down in a liquid
quiz.explain: When a mixture is left still, heavy particles like mud settle at the bottom.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up sedimentation with other methods

quiz.q: Pouring off clear water without disturbing the settled mud is called:
quiz.explain: Decantation means gently pouring the liquid away from the sediment.
quiz.mistake: Confuses decantation with filtration

quiz.q: Which method separates tea leaves from tea?
quiz.explain: A tea strainer is a filter: the liquid tea passes and the leaves stay.
quiz.mistake: Picks a method meant for dry mixtures

quiz.q: After filtering, the solid left on the filter paper is called the:
quiz.explain: The solid that stays on the filter is the residue; the liquid that passes is the filtrate.
quiz.mistake: Swaps residue and filtrate

quiz.q: Is filtered water always safe to drink?
options: No, it may still have germs, so it should be boiled or purified
quiz.explain: Germs are too tiny to be stopped by simple filters, so water must be boiled or purified.
quiz.mistake: Thinks clear-looking water is always safe

quiz.q: Which of these can be separated by sedimentation and decantation?
quiz.explain: Sand is insoluble and heavy, so it settles and the water can be poured off.
quiz.mistake: Thinks dissolved substances will settle

quiz.q: How is paneer separated from whey at home?
options: By filtering through a muslin cloth
By sieving with a chhalni for flour
quiz.explain: The muslin cloth lets the whey pass and holds back the paneer.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that a cloth works as a filter

quiz.q: Why is filtration usually done after sedimentation and decantation?
options: Most of the mud is removed first, so the filter does not get blocked quickly
Filtration must always be done first
quiz.explain: Removing most of the mud first means the filter only has to catch the smaller particles left behind.
quiz.mistake: Does not understand why methods are combined in an order

teach.ask: Gappu looks at a muddy puddle: 'I'm thirsty! How can I get the mud out of this water? Is clear water safe to drink?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Let the mud settle, pour off the water, filter it, and boil it before drinking. Clean water at last!
teach.nudge: After the mud settles, what do I do next? And is filtered water fully safe?

topics.title: Evaporation, churning and using methods together

learn.hook: How do we get salt from the salty sea? The Sun helps us do it!
points: Evaporation can separate a solid dissolved in water: when the water evaporates, the solid is left behind.
Salt is made this way in salt pans along the coasts of states like Gujarat: seawater is let into shallow pans and the Sun evaporates the water, leaving salt.
Churning: curd or cream is churned (stirred hard) with a mathani or a churner. Butter, which is lighter, collects on top and is separated from buttermilk (chhaas).
Sometimes we use more than one method. Salt and sand: add water to dissolve the salt, filter out the sand, then evaporate the water to get the salt back.
Safety: heating to evaporate should only be done by or with an adult.

example.q: Sana accidentally mixes salt with sand. How can she get both back?
steps: Add water and stir: salt dissolves, sand does not.
Filter the mixture: sand stays on the filter paper as residue.
Leave the salty filtrate in a shallow dish in the sun (or let an adult heat it) so the water evaporates.
Salt is left behind in the dish.
example.answer: Dissolve in water, filter to get the sand, then evaporate the water to get the salt.

learn.reallife: Making butter by churning curd is common in many Indian homes, and the leftover chhaas is a cool summer drink.

games.title: Which method separates it?
items: Salt from seawater
Sugar from sugar solution
Butter from curd
Butter from cream
Tea leaves from tea
Sand from sandy water
Paneer from whey

games.title: Separation facts
items: Salt can be got from seawater by evaporation.
The Sun evaporates the water in salt pans, leaving salt.
Filtration can separate salt dissolved in water.
Dissolved salt passes through the filter with the water.
Churning curd separates butter from buttermilk.
Butter is lighter and gathers on top while churning.
To get salt and sand back from a mixture, we can dissolve, filter and then evaporate.
Each method removes one part.
Children should heat salty water on a stove by themselves.
Heating should be done by or with an adult for safety.

quiz.q: How is salt obtained from seawater?
quiz.explain: The Sun evaporates the water from seawater in shallow pans, leaving salt behind.
quiz.mistake: Picks a method used for dry mixtures

quiz.q: Can filtration separate salt that is dissolved in water?
options: Yes, the salt stays on the filter paper
Yes, but only with a tea strainer
No, dissolved salt passes through the filter
quiz.explain: Dissolved particles are mixed in the water and go through the filter. Evaporation is needed.
quiz.mistake: Thinks filtration removes dissolved substances

quiz.q: Which method is used to get butter from curd?
quiz.explain: Churning makes the butter separate and collect on top.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the method of churning

quiz.q: What is the correct order to separate a mixture of salt and sand?
quiz.explain: Dissolving frees the salt into water, filtering removes the sand, and evaporating gives back the salt.
quiz.mistake: Puts the steps in the wrong order

quiz.q: Why does butter collect on top when curd is churned?
quiz.explain: Butter is lighter than buttermilk, so it floats up and gathers on top.
quiz.mistake: Thinks heavier parts rise

quiz.q: Sugar is dissolved in water. How can you get the sugar back?
quiz.explain: When the water evaporates, the sugar is left behind.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a filter can catch dissolved sugar

quiz.q: Where in India is salt commonly made from seawater?
options: In salt pans along the coast of Gujarat
On the snowy peaks of the Himalayas
In the middle of thick forests
quiz.explain: Coastal areas like Gujarat have salt pans where seawater evaporates in the sun.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect salt-making with the sea coast

quiz.q: What is left in the dish when salty water evaporates?
quiz.explain: The water turns to vapour and the dissolved salt stays behind.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the salt evaporates along with the water

teach.ask: Gappu tastes seawater: 'Yuck, salty! How do people get the salt out of the sea? And how does Nani get butter from curd?'
teach.praise: Wow! The Sun evaporates seawater and salt is left behind. And churning curd brings butter to the top!
teach.nudge: What happens to the water when the Sun heats it? And how is butter separated?
